Date: 2026-12-02

Duration: 47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jorge Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (NovaBank Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (NovaBank Security Engineer), Ravi Menon (IAM Admin), Sofia Martins (Compliance)
summary: High-level security review focusing on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model. Customer on Okta, wants automated provisioning into Redwood (SCIM), assertion and attribute mapping review, group sync for RBAC, audit log retention and encryption key controls. Agreement to run a provisioning test and exchange metadata and example payloads.
topics: SAML SSO: SP vs IdP init, cert rollover, ACS URLs
SCIM provisioning: endpoints, attribute mappings, group sync, delta vs full sync
RBAC model: admin/operator/viewer roles, least-privilege mapping from groups
Encryption and KMS/HSM for customer data at rest
transcript:
[00:00] Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick security review - mostly SSO, SCIM, and RBAC mapping. Aisha, can you kick off with where you are today?
[00:14] Aisha: Yeah thanks Morgan, so we're a NovaBank platform team, currently using Okta for SSO, and Syncro for user provisioning... sorry, not syncro, I mean we use Okta's SCIM connector. We also have Azure AD in a couple subsidiaries. Our main ask is automated provisioning into Redwood and a least-privilege role model for engineers versus ops
[00:36] Priya: Got it - and you're looking for SP-initiated or IdP-initiated flows?
[00:40] Liam: We're broadly IdP-initiated for the portal, but for automated test provisioning we might do SP-init. We have cert rotation policies every 90 days so we'd want to ensure cert rollover is smooth.
[00:53] Morgan: Yep we support both. We publish SP metadata and can consume IdP metadata, we also have a cert rollover doc. We'll send the SP metadata after this call.
[01:02] Ravi: On SCIM, how granular is the group sync? We want groups to map to RBAC roles so that when someone joins the "redwood-admins" group they get admin, and when they join "redwood-deploy" they get operator.
[01:16] Priya: We do group-based mappings. Our SCIM connector supports group members sync and delta updates. We also expose attributes: userName, name.familyName, name.givenName, emails[type=work], and custom schemas for roles. One note - some IdPs send group IDs instead of names, so we recommend mapping on group displayName or providing a transform.
[01:38] Liam: Okta in our setup sends group names by default but sometimes we've seen truncated names, so would be good to confirm attribute filters.
[01:46] Morgan: We'll share an attribute mapping spreadsheet. Priya, you have an example payload?
[01:50] Priya: Yes, I'll attach a sample SCIM POST for a user and a PATCH for group members. Example: POST /scim/v2/Users with schemas array, userName as email, and groups array with "display": "redwood-operator". There's also a GET /scim/v2/Groups to reconcile.
[02:12] Sofia: For compliance, what about audit logs and retention - we need 7 years retention for certain events and immutable logs for some datasets.
[02:22] Jorge: We currently retain audit logs for 1 year by default on hosted plan, but Redwood can offer extended retention on enterprise plans and support pushing audit events to your SIEM via syslog or a secure webhook. We also provide signed export snapshots for audit.
[02:40] Sofia: Can you confirm immutability or WORM support?
[02:45] Priya: We can export immutable logs to your S3 bucket with Vault lock if you require WORM; otherwise we provide append-only storage within our system and cryptographic checksums for exports. We'll follow up with exact architecture notes.
[03:02] Liam: Encryption - do you manage keys or can we bring our own KMS? We require customer-managed keys (CMK) for PII in production.
[03:10] Morgan: We support BYOK: you can supply a KMS key via AWS KMS or external HSM using KMIP for Private deployments. For hosted, we support AWS KMS CMKs and have HSM-backed options for enterprise. We'll note the supported algorithms (AES-256 for at-rest, TLS1.2+ in transit).
[03:28] Ravi: How is RBAC enforced? We have a strict least-privilege standard: infra team should not have access to data plane logs, only to deploy.
[03:36] Priya: RBAC in Redwood is role-based with scopes. Out-of-the-box roles: owner, admin, operator, viewer. Each role maps to API scopes and console privileges. We support custom roles on Dedicated/Private where you can define granular scopes like 'inference:invoke', 'models:deploy', 'billing:view'. Role assignment can be driven by SCIM group membership or via SAML assertion attributes (groups claim).
[04:00] Aisha: Can we do a policy where a role in Okta maps to tags/labels in Redwood and only users in the tagged groups can access certain model endpoints?
[04:08] Priya: Yes, we support attribute-based access tied to group claims. For more advanced constraints, we can do per-route policies through our Console and API. We'll send JSON role examples.
[04:20] Sofia: SOC2 scope - do you have SOC2 reports and encryption attestations?
[04:25] Morgan: Yes we're SOC2 Type II certified; we'll share the SOC2 pack under an NDA if needed, and our ISO readiness notes. We also maintain regular pen tests and vuln scans.
[04:36] Liam: Data residency - we need EU-only for some workloads. How do you guarantee region isolation for both data at rest and metadata?
[04:46] Morgan: We have region pinning for both Hosted and Dedicated; for EU-only we can ensure data and backups remain in eu-west-1 or customer-selected region. For Private you'll manage the infra. We'll provide our data residency policy document.
[04:58] Ravi: About SAML attributes - we need nameid to be persistent and mapped to employee id, also want to receive an "groups" claim with full list.
[05:08] Priya: Standard SAML assertion mapping: NameID (transient or persistent), email, givenName, familyName, and groups. We recommend persistent NameID for stable mapping. For SCIM provisioning we'll still use emails/userName as canonical.
[05:24] Liam: One tricky area is de-provisioning - we need immediate revoke of access when Okta deactivates a user. How fast is SCIM delta sync?
[05:31] Priya: Delta is near real-time when Okta pushes; typical latency is sub-minute. For extra safety we also honor SAML session expiration and token TTL.
[05:41] Aisha: Cert rollover - what happens to sessions during rotation?
[05:45] Morgan: We do a rolling cert swap with overlap window; sessions remain valid, new logins use new cert. We'll share our cert rotation playbook.
[05:56] Sofia: For audit, can we map actions to users with IP and device context?
[06:02] Priya: We capture actor, IP, timestamp, action and resource. Device context is limited to user agent and sometimes X-Forwarded-For; for richer device telemetry we recommend integrating with your SSO/XDR stack.
[06:18] Liam: Any limitations on groups number? We have thousands of groups across Okta.
[06:23] Priya: We support large group counts; with caveat on initial full sync which can be heavier - we recommend scoped group filters for the pilot. Deltas are efficient.
[06:34] Morgan: Let's talk about testing - propose a 1hr provisioning test: we will give SP metadata, you provide a test Okta app or metadata URL, we'll run create, update, deactivate flows and confirm role mapping.
[06:45] Aisha: Sounds good. Also can you confirm RBAC for service accounts? We have CI/CD system accounts that should have token-based access with reduced scopes.
[06:54] Priya: We have service principal support - token issuance tied to specific scopes and expiry. You can constrain by IP and set short TTLs.
[07:05] Ravi: Are there logs for service principal activity separate from user logs?
[07:09] Jorge: Yes we emit actor type (User vs Service) in logs and can filter exports.
[07:16] Sofia: Any legal paperwork for SOC2 - do you accept our standard DPA or do we need a CLA?
[07:24] Morgan: We have a standard DPA and can add SOC2 addendum. We'll circulate the legal pack after the call.
[07:32] Aisha: Ok next steps would be the provisioning test and exchange of metadata. Also send the mapping spreadsheet and RBAC JSON samples.
[07:41] Morgan: Agreed. We'll follow-up with dates. Thanks everyone.
[07:44] (meeting ended)
